questions.question: Q1 What is the primary purpose of photolithography in semiconductor manufacturing?

answers.b: To create circuit patterns on the wafer surface

explanations.a: Melting silicon is part of crystal growth, not photolithography.
explanations.b: Correct! Photolithography is used to transfer circuit patterns onto the wafer.
explanations.c: Crystal growth is performed before wafer fabrication.
explanations.d: Cutting wafers is done during packaging and dicing.

questions.question: Q2 What material is coated on the wafer before UV exposure?

explanations.a: Copper is mainly used for interconnections.
explanations.b: Correct! A photoresist layer is coated on the wafer surface.
explanations.c: Aluminum is not used as the coating material in this step.
explanations.d: Oxide dust is not used in photolithography.

questions.question: Q3 What is the role of the photomask in photolithography?

answers.c: It transfers the desired pattern using UV light

explanations.a: Heating is done during baking processes.
explanations.c: Correct! The photomask defines the pattern transferred to the wafer.
explanations.d: Wafer spinning is performed by the spin coater.

questions.question: Q4 Which source is commonly used to expose the photoresist?

explanations.a: Infrared light is not typically used for standard photolithography.
explanations.b: Correct! UV light is commonly used to expose photoresist.
explanations.c: Microwaves are not used for pattern transfer.
explanations.d: X-rays are used only in specialized lithography methods.

questions.question: Q5 What is the purpose of spin coating?

answers.b: To uniformly spread photoresist on the wafer

explanations.a: Spin coating does not remove silicon.
explanations.b: Correct! Spin coating creates a uniform photoresist layer.

questions.question: Q6 What is the purpose of the soft bake step?

answers.a: To remove solvents from the photoresist

explanations.a: Correct! Soft baking removes excess solvent and improves adhesion.
explanations.b: Oxide growth occurs in oxidation processes.
explanations.c: Etching is a separate fabrication step.

questions.question: Q7 What happens to the photoresist after proper UV exposure and development?

answers.a: A pattern is formed on the wafer

explanations.a: Correct! Exposure and development create the desired pattern.

questions.question: Q8 Which chemical is used to remove selected photoresist regions after exposure?

explanations.a: Correct! Developer solution dissolves the exposed or unexposed resist depending on resist type.
explanations.b: Nitrogen is generally used as a purge gas.
explanations.d: SiO₂ is not used as a developer.

questions.question: Q9 Why is alignment important before UV exposure?

answers.a: To ensure the pattern is transferred correctly

explanations.a: Correct! Proper alignment ensures accurate pattern placement.

questions.question: Q10 Which sequence correctly represents the photolithography process?

answers.b: Spin Coating → Soft Bake → UV Exposure → Development

explanations.b: Correct! This is the standard photolithography sequence.
explanations.d: Etching is performed after pattern creation.
